newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand was trading near the weaker end of its intraday range in quiet late Tuesday dealings.
At 1400 GMT the rand was changing hands at 4.4650/4680 to the dollar from Monday's late level of 4.4605/4635.
Traders said one import order for about $100 million did most of the damage, pummelling the unit steadily softer over the day despite early hopes for stability.

Exporter capacity to absorb the rand sell orders all but dried up around midday after the currency spent two-hours knocking on the 4.4650 ceiling, paving the way for an afternoon push toward the next resistance level at 4.4700.
Traders said some renewed interest from London and remaining scraps of local exporter demand were keeping the 4.4700 level safe from assault for the time being.
Late cross rate action saw the rand keeping most of its early gains against the Japanese yen with the unit last quoted at 26.6674/7077 from 26.5965/6256 yen late Monday.

Morning rand strength against the German mark didn't last and it's latest price was at 0.3798/3802 from 0.3813/3816 previously. Rand strength against sterling also was eroded and the pound last cost locals 7.2780/2873 rand from 7.2394/2487 before.
In bond dealings the benchmark R150 stood at 14.925 from Monday's late level of 14.965.

Dealers said the market was tracking U.S. debt futures movements in the absence of persuasive local factors but they noted Stateside debt traders seemed undecided as to the impact of earlier news of a 0.3 percent drop in April U.S. retail sales.
"The U.S. didn't do much. They (U.S. bonds) strengthened a bit and then they weakened again. We're fast going nowhere," said one dealer.
The R150 bond kept well clear of the 15.00 percent key psychological level and the 40-day moving average of 14.99 and was seen between 14.91-96 pct for the balance of the trading day.
Bond Exchange data showed foreigners offloaded local debt totalling 25.96 on Monday having bought 257.53 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday.
Nominal Bond Exchange turnover eased to 4.71 billion rand on Monday from 4.86 billion rand Friday.

In the money market, three month NCD rates from major banks lined up at 16.40 percent offered from their 16.40 to 16.45 percent range on Monday, while 90-day BA rates moved to between 15.90 and 15.96 percent from 15.80 to 15.95 percent previously.
The Reserve Bank reported the money market shortage broadly steady at 7.775 billion rand on Monday from 7.826 billion rand on Saturday.
